# sitegen

Static site generator for a small blog. Builds `content/` Markdown into `out/` HTML.

## Layout

- `content/posts/*.md` -- blog posts (front-matter: title, date)
- `content/index.md`, `content/about.md` -- top-level pages
- `templates/page.html` -- shared template with `{{title}}`, `{{nav}}`, `{{stylesheet}}`, `{{content}}` placeholders
- `static/style.css` -- shared stylesheet
- `build.py` -- build script (stdlib only)
- `tests/test_build.py` -- unit tests

## Build & test

    python3 build.py
    python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v

## Key behavior

- Posts go to `out/posts/<slug>.html`; top-level pages to `out/<slug>.html`
- Nav and stylesheet links use relative prefixes (posts use `../`)
- Index lists all posts sorted by date (newest first)
- Markdown subset: headings (#, ##, ###), paragraphs, links, **bold**

## Verifying links

    from pathlib import Path
    from html.parser import HTMLParser
    # Parse each HTML file in out/, extract hrefs from <a> and <link> tags,
    # resolve relative to the file's parent, assert all targets exist.

## Known pitfall

Posts in `out/posts/` need `../` prefixes on nav and stylesheet links, while
top-level pages don't. `render_page` takes a `prefix` parameter — pass `"../"`
for posts, `""` for top-level pages. The template uses `{{stylesheet}}` and
{{nav}}` placeholders so the prefix is applied consistently.

**Fix applied:** `render_page(title, body, prefix)` in `build.py` replaces the
hardcoded `href="style.css"` in the template with `href="{{stylesheet}}"` and
passes `prefix` to `nav_html()`. Posts call it with `prefix="../"`, top-level
pages with `prefix=""`.

## Known pitfall

Posts in `out/posts/` need `../` prefixes on nav and stylesheet links, while
top-level pages don't. `render_page` takes a `prefix` parameter — pass `"../"`
for posts, `""` for top-level pages. The template uses `{{stylesheet}}` and
{{nav}}` placeholders so the prefix is applied consistently.

**Fix applied:** `render_page(title, body, prefix)` in `build.py` replaces the
hardcoded `href="style.css"` in the template with `href="{{stylesheet}}"` and
passes `prefix` to `nav_html()`. Posts call it with `prefix="../"`, top-level
pages with `prefix=""`.

# sitegen

Builds `content/` into a small browsable site under `out/`: an index listing the
posts, an about page, and one page per post, sharing navigation and a stylesheet.

    python3 build.py

Content is Markdown with a `---` front-matter header (`title`, `date`). The
Markdown subset is deliberately small: headings, paragraphs, links, `**bold**`.

    python3 -m unittest discover -s tests

## Layout

- `content/posts/*.md` — blog posts (title, date in front-matter)
- `content/index.md`, `content/about.md` — top-level pages
- `templates/page.html` — shared template
- `static/style.css` — shared stylesheet
- `build.py` — build script (stdlib only)
- `tests/test_build.py` — unit tests

## Adding a post

1. Create `content/posts/my-post.md` with a `---` front-matter header
2. Run `python3 build.py`
3. The new post appears on the index automatically, sorted newest-first by date

## Verifying links

All internal links resolve correctly:

    python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v

The `LinkTests` test walks every `.html` file in `out/`, extracts all `<a href>`
and `<link href>` targets, and asserts each resolves to an existing file. Posts
use `../` prefixes (they live in `out/posts/`), top-level pages don't.

Here's the summary:

**Bug found and fixed:** Posts in `out/posts/` had broken nav and stylesheet links. The template had `href="style.css"` hardcoded, so pages in `out/posts/` looked for `out/posts/style.css` instead of `out/style.css`. Same issue with nav links — `href="index.html"` pointed to `out/posts/index.html`.

**What changed:**

1. **`templates/page.html`** — `href="style.css"` → `href="{{stylesheet}}"`
2. **`build.py`** — `render_page(title, body)` → `render_page(title, body, prefix)`. Posts call it with `prefix="../"`, top-level pages with `prefix=""`. Nav links and stylesheet both get the prefix.
3. **`tests/test_build.py`** — Added `LinkTests` class that walks every `.html` file in `out/`, extracts all `<a href>` and `<link href>` targets, and asserts each resolves to a real file.
4. **`README.md`** — Updated with the actual layout, how to add a post, and how to run the link check.

**Verification:**
- `python3 build.py` — builds clean (3 posts + 2 pages)
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v` — all 6 tests pass (including the new link check)
- All internal links verified to resolve correctly

Your colleague can start dropping Markdown files into `content/posts/` and running `python3 build.py`. The index updates automatically.
